floor_history.headline: Floor 16 -> 10 by deleting the inherited pins/barrier/volatile for clean pure C (RA now exact); residual is target's 8-byte phantom frame (2 insns) + 2 scheduling placements, and a >=4-byte local aggr

frontier.hypothesis: A >=4-byte local aggregate that is already SImode-shaped in its natural use will reproduce target's phantom frame at zero instruction cost, closing the 2-insn frame gap.
frontier.mechanism: The frame is confirmed reachable via assign_stack_local on a >=4-byte local aggregate (vars=8, zero traffic when it collapses to one forwarded pseudo). The only reason the union form loses is the mode-punning pack/unpack between its SImode pseudo and the two HImode halves the table wants. An aggregate whose members are s32/pointer-shaped has nothing to pack, so the tax disappears.
frontier.next_probe: Extend tmp/grind/func_80086014/s1/frame_probe.c with aggregates carrying word-shaped values consumed by the address arithmetic or the flag RMW rather than the s16 value pair: `struct { Slot16 *p; }`, `union { s32 off; u8 b[4]; }`, and a resized/retuned version of the round-3 `union {u8 b[4]; s32 w;}` flag variant (it already gave sp_traffic=0 but vars=0). Run run_probe.sh and select on vars=8 AND sp_traffic=0 AND insns<=16, then confirm with `sandbox func_80086014 --disable all`. The aggregate must stay live and load-bearing - an unused/unwritten one is the forbidden dead-local-array cheat and its carve-out gate fails here.

frontier.hypothesis: func_80047E5C's C body is a working in-tree pure-C recipe for a 27-instruction leaf with an 8-byte phantom frame, directly transplantable to func_80086014.
frontier.mechanism: Not a codegen hypothesis but an evidence lookup with the best cost/value ratio left: 21 already-matched functions demonstrably produce this frame from pure C under this exact toolchain, and this one matches both our frame signature and our instruction count.
frontier.next_probe: Run `engine build`, then map address 0x80047E5C to its owning object and symbol (build map, or objdump over build/src/*.o, or cross-reference bb2.ld), and read that C body. Repeat for the 11-insn func_8007DEE4 if the first is inconclusive. Feed whatever shape carries their frame back into the frame_probe.c grid.

frontier.hypothesis: The two remaining scheduling placements close by making the flag address data-dependent on the pair address, rather than by any barrier.
frontier.mechanism: cc1 sched1 hoists the flag lbu above the first sh because D_80102A7A and D_800F65E0 are distinct symbols and provably non-aliasing, leaving the scheduler free to launch the load early for latency; target issues it after the store. Same for `move v0,zero` floating to the block top. Serializing the addressing creates a real data dependence that pins the order without any coercion.
frontier.next_probe: Apply [[walking-pointer-serializes-parallel-loads]]: derive the pair address and the flag address from one walked/advanced pointer so the dependence is genuine. Worth ~2-3 of the 10 and lower priority than the frame - and it may fall out for free once the frame-carrying aggregate changes the dependence graph, so re-measure it AFTER the frame lands. Do NOT use a memory clobber or volatile; both are cheats and both were in the inherited body that scored worse.
